audit.why: 53.84% over 1614 games. An early-window lane: you are ahead until his resists and tank items land, then it inverts. The page already frames it that way and the level chart's mostly-Skill spread fits a lane decided by whether you cash the first five levels.

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item and late spikes both attribute the flip to a 'percent-HP passive'.
audit.why: Dauntless Instinct is not percent-health. Riot's text: 'K'Sante's Abilities mark targets to take more damage on his next Attack. When All Out, K'Sante deals more damage with all Attacks and Abilities.' It is an ability-into-auto mark, which is a burst tell you can step away from, not a scaling health-shred you have to itemise against. Twice on the page the player is told to fear a mechanic K'Sante does not have, and told nothing about the wind-up he actually telegraphs.
audit.corrected: Both spikes rewritten around Dauntless Instinct as a mark-then-attack tell, with Footwork's shield as the real reason his first item flips trades.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ntofo Strikes is called a 'Q knockup line' in four places, and Path Maker is called a 'W block' that only absorbs damage and dashes away.
audit.why: Both are wrong in the direction that gets you killed. Ntofo Strikes does not knock up: it 'damages and slows enemies in a short line', and at two stacks it 'fires a shockwave that pulls enemies in' — a pull, not a knockup, and pulls set up his all-in rather than interrupt it. It is also on a 3.5s cooldown flat, so 'block his Q' is not a plan; it is back up long before your Aegis Assault. And Path Maker is not a block: he 'charges up, taking reduced damage, then dashes, knocking back and stunning enemies'. It is an engage that stuns you, and the page presents it purely as an escape. That stun is also what cancels your Aegis Assault mid-channel.
audit.corrected: Ntofo Strikes restated as a slowing line that pulls at two stacks on 3.5s, and Path Maker restated as a charge-and-stun engage on 14s that cancels your channel.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers on a page whose whole plan is 'bait his W'.
audit.why: Path Maker is 14/13/12/11/10s and Footwork 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s — the two windows worth waiting for. Against your Shield Vault at 13s down to 9s the trade is close to one-for-one. All Out is 120/100/80s.
audit.corrected: Path Maker and Footwork cooldowns written into the spikes, wants and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal and no note on why armour underperforms.
audit.why: All Out heals him for the duration, so Grievous Wounds decides every post-6 extended fight. Path Maker carries true damage, which armour does not reduce — the page says his resists climb but never that part of his damage ignores yours.
audit.corrected: Both written into the late text.

edits.before: Point-and-click W stun into Q burst is your hardest level-1/2 window — K'Sante's W block is on cooldown if you bait it, so all-in before he has it back.
edits.after: Shield Vault into Comet Spear is your hardest level-1/2 window — Path Maker is 14s and it stuns, so bait it out first and all-in inside that window.

edits.before: Empowered-Q (Mortal Will) poke plus E's directional block shut off his Q knockup line — chip his huge HP bar before his per-level resists make trades unprofitable.
edits.after: Ntofo Strikes slows in a line and pulls you in at two stacks, and it is only 3.5s — poke with empowered Comet Spear and chip his HP bar before his resists climb.

edits.before: K'Sante's first tank item (Hullbreaker/Heartsteel/Black Cleaver) flips the duel — his percent-HP passive starts shredding you faster than your Eclipse/Profane burst can answer.
edits.after: K'Sante's first tank item flips the duel — Footwork's shield on 10s plus Dauntless Instinct marking you for a bigger attack now beats your Eclipse or Profane burst outright.

edits.before: Hold W to block your Q poke and dash away from your W-stun all-in
edits.after: Charge Path Maker, then dash in to knock you back and stun the channel

edits.before: Bait his W block/dash, then W-stun in and Q-burst before it is back up
edits.after: Bait Path Maker, then Shield Vault in and burst inside its 14 seconds

edits.before: Your full combo (W-stun, Q, E-block) threatens a kill, yet his Q knockup and W dash give him a clean out if he respects you — genuinely even.
edits.after: Your full combo threatens a kill, but Ntofo Strikes pulls you in at two stacks and Path Maker stuns the channel — genuinely even.

edits.before: K'Sante's first tank item plus his percent-HP passive flips the duel — his damage now outpaces your Eclipse/Profane burst.
edits.after: His first tank item plus Footwork's 10s shield flips the duel — his damage now outpaces your Eclipse or Profane burst.

edits.before: K'Sante is squishiest right now — before his per-level resists and tank items show up, his big HP bar is just a target. At level 1 your point-and-click W stun plus Mortal Will-empowered Q does real damage to him; bait his W block out first since it absorbs your Q, then W in and burst. Use E's directional block to eat his Q knockup line and his autos cleanly, and chip him with the long thrown Q so you're ahead before he stabilizes.
edits.after: K'Sante is squishiest right now — before his resists and tank items, his big HP bar is just a target. Shield Vault plus a Mortal Will-empowered Comet Spear does real damage. Bait Path Maker first: he charges up taking reduced damage, then dashes in to knock you back and stun, so it is an engage, not an escape, and it is 14s at rank 1. Face Aegis Assault at Ntofo Strikes for the damage, and chip him with the thrown spear before he stabilises.

edits.before: This is still your lane, but it's tightening. Keep poking with empowered-Q and farming at range — his Q knockup is his only real engage, and your E blocks it from one direction. Respect that his per-level resists are climbing, so each all-in does a little less; pick your W-in for when his W block is on cooldown. At 6, use Grand Starfall to roam rather than to win the 1v1 — your map pressure converts your lead while it still matters, because his late game is coming.
edits.after: Still your lane, but tightening. Poke with empowered Comet Spear and farm at range. Do not plan around blocking Ntofo Strikes — it is 3.5s flat, back up long before Aegis Assault, and the two-stack shockwave pulls you in rather than pushing you off. Path Maker is the one to count at 14s, because its stun cancels your channel outright and Aegis Assault only covers your front anyway. Shield Vault in while it is down. At 6, roam with Grand Starfall instead of duelling.

edits.before: Be honest: K'Sante out-scales you hard. Once he has two tank items his percent-HP passive and R-strip turn the duel decisively his way — he isolates you, strips his own resists for the all-in, and your damage plateaus while his sustain and HP balloon. Do not 1v1 him after items. Win the lane and the map in the first 15 minutes through roams and objectives, then group and let your team absorb him while you clean up the squishies he can't reach.
edits.after: Be honest: K'Sante out-scales you hard. All Out knocks you back through a wall and then dashes after you, so he picks the ground and you fight him alone — and it heals him, so Grievous Wounds is not optional after 6. Path Maker carries true damage, so stacking armour reads that trade wrong. Do not 1v1 him after items. Win the map in the first 15 minutes with roams and objectives, then group and clean up the squishies he cannot reach.

notes: Two mechanics were described backwards, both in the direction that gets a Pantheon killed. Ntofo Strikes was called a 'Q knockup line' four times; Riot's text is 'damages and slows enemies in a short line' and at two stacks 'fires a shockwave that pulls enemies in'. A pull sets up his all-in — the page told you it interrupts one. It is also 3.5s flat, so the repeated advice to block it with a 22-second Aegis Assault does not work arithmetically. Path Maker was called a 'W block' he dashes away with; Riot's text has him charge up taking reduced damage and then dash in 'knocking back and stunning enemies'. It is his engage, and it is what cancels your channel. Third, Dauntless Instinct was called a 'percent-HP passive' twice; it marks targets to take more damage on his next attack. Level chart left alone — mostly Skill is honest for a lane this dependent on cashing the first five levels.
